directions.title: INTERVAL-HINT: the trace-set filter is exact (2^-omega pruning) but does not amplify — residue filters fully closed
directions.description:
**Paper 51 (NewMathematics) — Experiment 386, assessment v162. Round-14 #9.**

**Hypothesis:** can the FREE trace-set filter (TRACEPROFILE) amplify an external interval hint s in [s0-E, s0+E]?

**Experiment (400 semiprimes, k=24 / 48-bit N; trace-set + p-set filters omega=0-20 primes; rejection-ordered scan with honest Delta/membership accounting):**

1. **Trace-set filter is EXACT:** true s survives 400/400 at every omega<=20; wrong s' pruned by EXACTLY 2^-omega(M#) (0.1233 vs 0.125 at omega=3; 0.0151 vs 0.0156 at omega=6).
2. **p-filter EMPTY for real candidates:** coprime survival = 1.0000 — only coprimality, which primes already satisfy (candidate-level zero-block).
3. **No amplification:** Delta-tests drop 8001 -> 121.5/2.9/1.1 (omega=6/12/18, exactly (2E+1)*2^-omega+1) but are replaced by ~1.9 membership-tests/candidate (15 294-15 550) — cost parity or worse; full range still iterated.
4. **No-hint search exponentially sealed:** survivors 2^24 -> 2^19 -> 2^13.3 -> 2^7.4 (omega=0/6/12/18); poly would need M# ~ e^(k ln k), super-exponential — trace-set is Omega(N)-sealed (barrier 2/4).
5. **s-scan IS Fermat in disguise** (barrier 8).

**Verdict:** refutes the last residue-amplification hope. Even the least-hidden invariant's filter is an exact but information-useless consistency certificate. Together with DIAL-THRESHOLD and QRLEAK/COMPENSATING-PARTNER, the residue-filter family (on factor, order, and trace) is now completely closed.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/51_IntervalHint_ExactFilterNoAmplification.md

directions.title: TRACEPROFILE: the trace s=p+q is the least-hidden symmetric invariant — 1 bit per prime exactly, s1=1-N1 theorem
directions.description:
**Paper 50 (NewMathematics) — Experiment 385, assessment v161. Round-14 #7.**

**Hypothesis:** the trace s = p+q (minimal factor-bearing witness) has a different information profile than the factor p — congruence-visible where p is congruence-invisible.

**Experiment (k=12,14; 32 640–380 628 semiprime pairs; mod-m MI, CRT trace-set sizes, full pairwise bit matrix):**

1. **Factor invisible, trace constrained EXACTLY:** I(p mod m; N mod m) ~ 0 for all m (zero-block extends to odd m); I(s mod m; N mod m) = 1.0000 bits at m=3, ~1.03–1.06 per odd prime, because s mod m is pinned to the trace-set {x+y mod m : xy=N} of size (m+1)/2.
2. **JOINT LAW: exactly one bit per prime.** |S_{M#}|/M# = 2^{-omega(M#)} exactly (0.5011, 0.2509, 0.1260, ... each prime halves it) -> I(s mod M#; N) = omega(M#) bits, additively independent.
3. **EXACT LOW-BIT THEOREM: s_1 = 1 - N_1** (holds 300000/300000 pairs; N_1 = p_1+q_1 mod 2, s_1 = p_1+q_1+1 mod 2). Partial: s_2 != N_2 with prob 0.754.
4. **Trace is less superdense:** pairwise 2.32 bits vs H(s) = 12.6 -> 18.5–21.9% visible (factor: 5%), in exact low-bit relations + top-2 carry-out sliver.

**Verdict:** the trace is the least-hidden symmetric invariant — the most accessible residue target — yet its visible bits are symmetric, cannot scale to pin s (needs M# >> e^{2^k}), and never isolate p or q. Barrier 2 + trace lemma confirmed at the information level. Not a factoring tool.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/50_TraceProfile_LeastHiddenInvariant.md

directions.title: EMPIRICAL-DEGREE: the factoring function is spectrally flat — no low-degree parity of N approximates any factor bit; the j=2 anomaly resolves as a symmetric top-bit fluctuation
directions.description:
**Paper 53 (NewMathematics) — Experiment 388, assessment v164. Round-14 #12.**

**Hypothesis:** f_j(N) = bit j of the smaller k-bit factor p, over the exact k-bit-prime semiprime support, has no low-degree GF(2) parity of N approximating it — the Walsh/spectral face of superdensity (BITPROFILE, barrier 1/2 probe).

**Experiment (restricted Walsh spectrum W(S) = sum_x f_j(x)(-1)^(S.x) by vectorized FWHT at k=10,12; targeted degree<=3 scans at k=14; m = 276/2850/32640/380628; random-sign null calibrated per size):**

1. **Spectral flatness CONFIRMED:** at k=14 every information-bearing bit below the top ~6 has max degree<=3 correlation <= 0.021 vs all-parity noise 0.0101 and degree<=3 null max 0.0065. No parity of <=3 bits of N approximates any factor bit.
2. **The only non-flat structure is the symmetric top-bit magnitude/carry family:** corr(p_{k-d}, N_{2k-1}) converges to ~0.285 (carry-out), 0.310, 0.132, 0.065, 0.026 for d=2..6 — the Walsh face of the BITPROFILE top-2 sliver, N-computable, symmetric in (p,q), a size correlation, non-factor-revealing.
3. **The round-1 "j=2 anomaly" (0.166 at k=10, ~1.7x noise) RESOLVED:** single-bit winner = N_{2k-1} (product-magnitude indicator); corr(p_2, N_{2k-1}) = 0.254/0.166/0.013/0.006 at k=8/10/12/14 — a small-k fluctuation of the symmetric top-bit family decaying into the noise floor.
4. **Low-half cubics decay:** corr(f_3,{1,2,3}) = 0.203->0.013, corr(f_4,{1,3,4}) = 0.145->0.009 across k=8..14 — finite-prime equidistribution effects at the 1/sqrt(#primes) scale (~1e-3 bits), qualifying the zero-block theorem over the prime-restricted support (exact over the full-odd support).
5. **Controls calibrate:** null (deg<=3) max 0.074/0.0213/0.0065 at k=10/12/14; constants j=0,k-1 trivially 1.0; carry-out j=k-2 reproduces at 0.51 linear/0.79 quadratic.

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED negative with positive content — the factoring function is as far from a low-degree parity approximator as a random function on its support, except for the symmetric size/carry structure N itself reveals. The k=10 j=2 anomaly and low-half cubics are small-k finite-prime fluctuations decaying with k. Barriers 1/2 (no low-degree GF(2) approximator; all N-computable structure symmetric). Closes the Walsh/GF(2) face of the barrier framework.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/53_EmpiricalDegree_SpectralFlatness.md

directions.title: SMOOTH-SELFHINT-DENSITY: the p-1/ECM weakness is residue-invisible — asymmetric/symmetric divisibility dichotomy, self-hint program closed
directions.description:
**Paper 54 (NewMathematics) — Experiment 389, assessment v165. Round-14 #10.**

**Hypothesis:** whether the smaller factor p has p-1 B-smooth (the weakness Pollard p-1 / ECM exploit) is detectable from N alone — a statistical instance-class self-hint (frontier iii).

**Experiment (random k-bit semiprimes, k=14/16/18, m to 200k; L(p-1)/L(q-1)/L(N-1)/L(N+1) via factorint; per-prime + joint MI with shuffled nulls; even-adjusted Dickman baseline; conditional densities):**

1. **Asymmetric residue leak is ZERO:** I(N mod l; l|p-1) = 0.0000–0.0005 bits at the shuffled-null level for l=3/5/7/11 at every k — N cannot tell which factor is ≡ 1 mod l.
2. **The SYMMETRIC event leaks strongly:** I(N mod l; l|p-1 OR l|q-1) = 0.313/0.036/0.015/0.005 bits (l=3/5/7/11), stable across k. Mechanism exact at l=3: N ≡ 2 mod 3 forces one factor ≡ 1 mod 3 (P(OR)=1.000) while P(p≡1|N mod 3) = 0.497/0.501 = base 0.499. The **asymmetric/symmetric divisibility dichotomy** — symmetry visible, asymmetry uncomputable from N (barrier 2 at the divisibility level).
3. **Full B-smoothness undetectable:** I(S_1000; N mod 1155) = 0.006 bits ≈ shuffled null 0.005.
4. **No instance-class self-hint:** N-1/N+1 smoothness (N-computable) does not predict factor smoothness (corr ≤ 0.014, MI ≤ 0.0001).
5. **Density conditioning-invariant and understood:** P(L(p-1)≤B | N mod l = n) = base for every n; base rate matches rho_even(log(2^k/2)/log B) within ~0.04 (powers-of-2 effect). ~60–78% of these semiprimes are 1000-weak — why p-1 works at all — yet the weak ones cannot be flagged from N.

**Verdict:** REFUTED as a self-hint in every form — the p-1/ECM-weak instance class is undetectable from N. CONFIRMED a sharp positive: the asymmetric/symmetric divisibility dichotomy quantifies barrier 2 at the divisibility level. Together with QRLEAK/COMPENSATING-PARTNER, DIAL-THRESHOLD, INTERVAL-HINT: the self-hint program is fully closed — no residue, dial, filter, or statistical smoothness self-hint exists; hints must be genuinely external (frontier iii complete). Barriers 2/5/8.

Full paper: ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/54_SmoothSelfHint_DensityInvisible.md

directions.title: Exp 390 GENERIC-RECOVERY: recovery-from-hint = 2^(k-1-t_eff) — hint taxonomy closed
directions.description:
**GENERIC-RECOVERY (round-14 #11, experiment 390, assessment v166, paper 55).**

Hypothesis: recovery of p from a t-bit external hint is bounded by the hint's usable information. Verified on exact k-bit-prime sets (k=14-25) and random semiprimes (k=16-20):

1. **Generic hints information-exact**: t-bit random GF(2) linear form of p's bits partitions P_k into classes |P_k|/2^t EXACTLY (k=16: 1515/759/190/48.6/12.8 vs 1515/757.5/189.4/47.3/11.8 at t=1..8); recovery cost = |P_k|/2^t (median steps = candidates). No anomalous class = no super-resolution.
2. **Value-hints parity-constrained** (new mini-finding): mod-2^t multiplicative c·p and XOR-mask hashes output only 2^(t-1) values (p odd) — class 378.9 vs 189.4 at k=16,t=4. Bit-vector forms are the only full-2^t generic hints.
3. **Trace hint sub-bit by recovery cost** (new positive): s mod 2^t pins p mod 2^t to C_t = O(1) roots (median saturating 4-8), but recovery tries all C_t: cost C_t·|P_k|/2^(t-1), measured 399 vs 47.3 (k=16,t=6), 354 vs 42.0 (k=18,t=8) — ~4.5-5x worse per bit; log2(C_t) ~ 3 bits lost to the root ambiguity.
4. **Only amplification = position**: crossing with pi(sqrt N) at t ~ k/2-3 for every family; the unique amplification is Coppersmith's contiguous top-half >= k/2 LLL (a known method, barrier 8). The Coppersmith condition is about POSITION, not the dial (DIAL-THRESHOLD revisited).

**Verdict**: CONFIRMED, sharpened. Hint taxonomy CLOSED: a t-bit external hint reduces the prime search by exactly 2^t, never more, never position-free; N-checkable hints are sealed at the trace-set floor (INTERVAL-HINT); hints must be genuinely external and worth their bits at face value. Barriers 4/8/2.

Script: /tmp/exp_genericrecovery.py. Paper: ResearchOutput/NewMathematics/55_GenericRecovery_HintTaxonomy.md

directions.title: Exp 392 GCD-MOMENT: the semiprime gcd-moments M_k = sum gcd(x,N)^k are a closed trace-witness family — trace recoverable, never a factor (barriers 2/4/6/8)
directions.description:
## GCD-MOMENT (exp 392, round-15 #1): the semiprime gcd-moments M_k = Σ_{x≤N} gcd(x,N)^k are a closed trace-witness family

**Hypothesis tested.** The brainstorm's S2 = N²+3N+1+(N−1)s−s² recovers the trace s = p+q via an O(N) prefix mean. Does any moment k escape the free-witness barriers?

**Result: CONFIRMED negative for factoring** (script: `/tmp/exp_gcdmoment.py`, verified by full enumeration 48/48 at k=1..4, 12/12 at k=5,6, plus symbolic expansion).

**1. Exact closed forms in (N, s) alone (verified).** Via the Newton power sums P_j = p^j+q^j = s·P_{j−1} − N·P_{j−2}:
> M_k = Σ_{x≤N} gcd(x,N)^k = Σ_{d|N} d^k φ(N/d) = **N^k + N·P_{k−1} − P_k + N − s + 1**

| k | M_k |
|---|-----|
| 1 | 4N − 2s + 1 |
| 2 | N² + 3N + 1 + (N−1)s − s² (= S2) |
| 3 | N³ − 2N² + N s² + 3N s + N − s³ − s + 1 |
| 4 | N⁴ − 3N²s − 2N² + N s³ + 4N s² + N − s⁴ − s + 1 |

**2. Trace recovery is unique at every k.** Roots of P_k(s)−M_k = 0: k=1 {s}; k=2 {s, N−1−s}; k=3 {1−s, s, N−1}; k=4 {s, N+1}+complex. s is ALWAYS the unique root in (0, N/2] — all spurious roots are ≥ N−1−s > N/2 or negative, so the size cut s < N/2 disambiguates trivially. (The "root ambiguity grows with k" worry resolves to a non-issue; the cost is computing M_k.)

**3. The genuine hierarchy is cost: N^{2k−1} samples to pin s.** Var(gcd(U,N)^k) ~ N^{2k−1} (the 1/N chance of gcd=N contributes N^k). Measured samples for s±1: k=1 ~4N (= the barrier-4 Ω(N) floor), k=2 ~N³, k=3 ~N⁵, k=4 ~N⁷. **k=1 = M1 = 4N−2s+1, an O(N) gcd-scan, is the optimal moment** — higher k are exponentially worse.

**4. Barriers: 2/4/6/8.**
- **Barrier 2 (symmetry):** M_k = F_k(N, s) for all k — p,q enter only through s and N. s alone never splits N; the trace is the ceiling of what a symmetric free witness can carry.
- **Barrier 4 (free-witness aggregation):** Ω(N) gcd evaluations; sampling no better (k=1 ~4N).
- **Barrier 6 (circular):** divisor form needs the factorization; closed form needs s; enumeration is Ω(N).
- **Barrier 8 (known method):** M1 = Σ_{d|N} d·φ(N/d) is the classical gcd-sum / Jordan-totient identity; the whole family is a known-arithmetic-function specialization.

**Reconfirms** TRACEPROFILE ("trace least-hidden") and QUERYWIT (threshold = Θ(p+q)): the trace s = p+q is the least-hidden — and here provably the ceiling — symmetric free witness, and it does not factor.

directions.title: Exp 391 BERGGREN-PRICE-INTERLOCK: every semiprime is a node of both Pythagorean trees — the N-node identity is exact, the interlock is factoring-orthogonal
directions.description:
**BERGGREN-PRICE-INTERLOCK (direct analysis request, experiment 391, assessment v167, paper 56).**

Hypothesis (refining the prior hypotenuse-N probe): the correct factoring-relevant embedding of N is not m^2+n^2 = N but ODD-LEG-N — the node (m,n) = ((p+q)/2, (q-p)/2), the Fermat pair. Verified on all valid (m,n) (BFS to L=11 both trees), 1020/1020 random semiprime pairs, and random 14-23-bit primes:

1. **N-NODE IDENTITY (new, exact, 1020/1020):** every odd semiprime N = pq is a valid node of BOTH the Berggren and Price trees at (m,n) = ((p+q)/2,(q-p)/2), with odd leg m^2-n^2 = (m-n)(m+n) = pq = N EXACTLY (hyp (p^2+q^2)/2, even leg (q^2-p^2)/2; p = m-n, q = m+n). Both trees enumerate all Fermat decompositions exactly once (3^L levels, parents invert with 0 failures). Factoring N == finding the N-node.
2. **Interlock = inequivalence over a shared vertex set:** Berggren child-map dets {+1,-1,+1} (subtract-2/reflect CF descent) vs Price {+2,-2,+2} (halving/binary-GCD descent) — no conjugacy (|det| invariant). Leg swap a<->b IS an automorphism of Berggren (S·B·S permutes {B1,B2,B3}, 3/3) but NOT of Price (0/3) — asymmetric. B-parent = P-parent on exactly 2/455,736 nodes.
3. **Depth duality:** dB (Berggren) ratio/CF-driven, erratic — N-node at 20-bit primes: mean 78.5, range [19,1135]; dP (Price) size-driven, tight — ~1.4·log2(p+q), sd ~2.4 (means 17.7/21.4/25.8/30.1 at 14/17/20/23-bit primes); corr(dB,dP) = -0.16 (independent orderings).
4. **Factoring verdict (decisive negative):** tree-work to find the N-node = 3^dB beat Fermat's scan in 0/209 trials at 20-bit primes (Fermat mean 6,630 steps; min case 3^19 ~ 1.2e9). dB correlates NEGATIVELY with Fermat cost (r = -0.31) — the trees measure the OPPOSITE of Fermat hardness (the ratio (p+q)/(q-p); Fermat cost ~ (q-p)^2/(8·sqrt N)); dP is size-blind (corr ~ 0). The root->N path string IS the factorization; no N-only branch rule; no pruning (odd legs ~constant along staircase branches); leg-only descent not closed. Hypotenuse density m^2+n^2 == 0 mod N in both trees <= 4/N, exactly 0 for N=15,21,35,77,91 (primitive pairs).

**Verdict:** CONFIRMED negative for factoring. The Pythagorean-tree line closes with exact statements: every odd semiprime sits at its Fermat pair in both trees (odd leg = N exactly — the correct embedding), the interlock is two inequivalent Euclidean descents over one vertex set, and traversal to the N-node costs 3^d >> Fermat's d_F (0/209). The trees organize the RATIO (p+q)/(q-p) — Fermat's ease coordinate — not the product pq; the ratio<->product map is the factorization step. Barriers 5/8 (structural orthogonality sharpened; the tree is Fermat in a different order). Scripts: /tmp/exp_berggrenprice.py, _3, _4.

directions.title: Exp 399 PLUSONE-SMOOTH-NULL (round-16 #2): the Williams p+1 weakness is residue-invisible, Lucas-sequence-invisible, and discriminant-gated
directions.description:
**PLUSONE-SMOOTH-NULL** — factoring research lab round-16 #2 (paper 64, assessment v175, 399 experiments). CONFIRMED null.

The Williams p+1 / Lucas-sequence weakness — the sibling of the p−1/ECM weakness (closed by SMOOTH-SELFHINT-DENSITY, SEQSMOOTH-NULL) — is invisible from N in three independent senses, plus a new structural finding.

1. **Positive control (classes genuinely differ):** 40 matched pairs (bit-lengths 18/21, only the smaller factor's p+1 divisibility differs); the p+1 method (M = lcm(1..100), bases 3/5/7) factors PLUSONE (p+1 | M) 24/40 vs GENERAL (p±1, q±1 general) 0/40. P=2 is the degenerate base (D=0).
2. **Residue-invisible:** I(N mod ℓ; ℓ|p+1) = 0.0005/0.0002/0.0014/0.0017/0.0022 at ℓ=3/5/7/11/13 (at or below null), while the symmetric control I(N mod ℓ; ℓ|p+1 OR ℓ|q+1) = 0.2996/0.0327/0.0158/0.0070/0.0052 is visible — the **+1 divisibility dichotomy** (mirror of the p−1 side's 0.313 at ℓ=3): N cannot tell which factor is ≡ −1 mod ℓ.
3. **Lucas-sequence-invisible:** 21 windowed V-sequence features (m=256, bases 3/5/7) separate the classes at chance — max std-diff 0.241 below the null mean 0.381, p = 0.898.
4. **NEW — discriminant gating:** per-base p+1 success EQUALS the (D|p) = −1 rate exactly (P=3: 11/40=11/40, P=5: 17/40=17/40, P=7: 11/40=11/40; 24/24 successes have (D|p)=−1; D₃=5 and D₇=45=5·3² share a square class → P=3,7 succeed on the same 11 instances), yet the N-computable product (D|N)=(D|p)(D|q) predicts nothing ((D|N)=−1 in 11/24 ≈ 1/2 of successes) — **the character split is uncomputable from N**, so the +1 weakness is strictly more hidden than the p−1 one.

**Verdict:** barriers 2/4/8. The weakness is real but exploitable only by running the classical 1982 method (barrier 8), never by inspecting N (barriers 2/4). **The ECM-family (p±1) self-hint program is fully closed.**
